title: Duelist's Handbook
subtitle: Dueling, collecting, commands and settings
intro: Click a chapter in the contents to go there. Turn pages with the arrows, the arrow keys or the mouse wheel; the line at the top of each page leads back to the contents.
Blue commands can be clicked, green values are this world's settings.

chapters.title: Getting started
text: On your first join you pick your **first deck**: Yugi's or Kaiba's starter deck, or a starter or structure deck that is already out. It comes in a deck box, ready to duel with. "Later" puts it off; `{cmd} starter` opens the choice again until you take one.
Then craft a **Duel Disk** and wear it in its Curios slot, or in your off hand without Curios.
[recipe {modid}:duel_disk]
Your first duel: `{cmd} duel bot` duels the computer right away. To duel a friend, both wear a disk and one right-clicks the other.
This book is given once on your first join. `{cmd} guide` opens it any time, and a new one is crafted from a book and paper.
[recipe {modid}:guide_book]

chapters.title: Dueling
text: # Challenging someone
- With a Duel Disk on, right-click another duelist. They right-click you back or click [Accept] in chat, and both disks unfold before the field appears.
- `{cmd} duel <player>` challenges by name, `{cmd} accept` takes the last challenge.
- `{cmd} duel bot` duels the computer.
# Ante duels

Sneak while right-clicking, or `{cmd} duel <player> ante`. Each duelist puts up a random card from their deck box and the winner takes both. The server keeps the cards until the duel ends, so a crash returns them.
# Two against two
- `{cmd} tag <partner> <opponent1> <opponent2>`: a tag duel. Partners share life points and the field and take turns with their own decks. Any seat can be `bot`.
- `{cmd} battlecity <partner> <opponent1> <opponent2>`: like a tag duel, but each partner plays on their own half of the team's zones.
# During a duel
You stand still and safe at your end of the field: nothing hurts you and mobs leave you alone. Surrender from the duel menu (Escape) or with `{cmd} forfeit`.
# Field Spells

A face-up Field Spell transforms its owner's half of the field: **Umi**, A Legendary Ocean and Umiiruka flood it with waves, **Yami** covers it in shadow, **Sogen** grows grass in the wind, Wasteland, Mountain, Forest, Gaia Power, Molten Destruction, Necrovalley, Rising Air Current, Luminous Spark and Mystic Plasma Zone each have their own ground. Other Field Spells tint the field in the colour of their attribute. With only one Field Spell out, it covers the whole field.
# Watching

Everyone within about 48 blocks of a duel sees its field in the world, with only the public cards. Right-click that field, someone who is dueling (NPCs too) or use `{cmd} watch <player>` to watch it up close. Spectators see the field, the life points and the log, but no hidden cards. Leave with Escape and "Stop watching" or `{cmd} unwatch`.
# Wins and losses

Every duel counts in your record: wins, losses and draws against players and against NPCs and bots, and your wins in a row. The result screen shows it, `{cmd} stats` in chat, `{cmd} stats <player>` someone else's and `{cmd} stats top` the ten best.

- Beating a player brings {server:results.players.winPacks} packs, {server:results.players.winPoints} DP, {server:results.players.winEmeralds} emeralds and {server:results.players.winXp} XP; losing {server:results.players.lossPacks} packs, {server:results.players.lossPoints} DP, {server:results.players.lossEmeralds} emeralds, {server:results.players.lossXp} XP.

- Beating an NPC brings {server:results.npcs.winPacks} packs, {server:results.npcs.winPoints} DP, {server:results.npcs.winEmeralds} emeralds and {server:results.npcs.winXp} XP; losing {server:results.npcs.lossPacks} packs, {server:results.npcs.lossPoints} DP, {server:results.npcs.lossEmeralds} emeralds, {server:results.npcs.lossXp} XP.
# Ranked duels

`{cmd} duel <player> ranked` (add `ante` for both) challenges someone to a ranked duel. Ranked duels win and lose rating points: everyone starts at {server:ranking.startRating}, beating someone rated higher brings more, and your first {server:ranking.placementGames} ranked duels count double. Only 1v1 duels between two players are ranked.
- **Ranks:** Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond and Duel King. Reaching a rank for the first time in a season brings {server:ranking.promotionPoints} DP.
- **{key:ranking}** or `{cmd} rank` opens the ranking window: your rank, the way to the next one and the best duelists. The result screen shows your new rating, and the player list (Tab) your rank.
- The same two players count {server:ranking.maxPerPairPerDay} ranked duels a day at most (0 means no limit).
- A **Ranking Board** on a wall shows the ten best on a glowing board three blocks wide and two high, above and beside it. Right-click it for the ranking window.
[recipe {modid}:ranking_board]
# Which deck you play
Your first legal deck box, looking in your hands first, then your inventory. Without one you duel with Yugi's starter deck, unless the server turned that off.

chapters.title: Duel controls
text: In a duel the camera looks down on the field and you play with the mouse.
- **Your hand** runs along the bottom. Click a card for its actions (Normal Summon, Set, Activate...) or drag it straight onto a zone.
- **Phase buttons** on the right show the phase: DP SP M1 BP M2 EP. Click BP, M2 or EP to go there.
- **Responses** open their own window, showing what you respond to. Pick a response or "Don't respond"; "-" folds it away.
- **Card details:** the card under the mouse is shown big on the left with its text and current ATK/DEF. Long text gets a scroll bar: turn the mouse wheel (anywhere but the duel log) or drag the bar.
- **Piles:** click a graveyard, the banished cards or an extra deck (right-click when a card there can be activated) to look through it.
- **Picks** on the field are made right there and confirmed with Confirm; picks from a pile open a card window.
# Keys
- **{key:duel_camera}**: top-down or first-person view. Hold the right mouse button to look around.
- **{key:duel_log}**: the duel log (scroll with the mouse wheel).
- **{key:duel_responses}**: be asked to respond, or pass every response you don't have to take.
- **{key:ranking}** (outside a duel): the ranking window.
- **{key:clan}** (outside a duel): the clan window.
- **{key:quests}** (outside a duel): your daily and weekly quests.
- **Space**: pass a response, confirm a pick or go to the next phase.
- **Enter**: confirm a pick. **1 to 9**: pick a plain answer.
- **Escape**: the duel menu (camera, responses, surrender, game menu).
Keys can be changed in Options > Controls; this page shows your current ones.

chapters.title: Collecting cards
text: Cards come from sealed products, opened like the real thing:
- **Booster Packs**: a core booster has 9 cards (one rare or better until 2014, a rare and a foil after), a tournament pack 3, mini boosters and battle packs 5.

Opening a booster pack is a show: click the pack to tear it open, the cards fan out face down, and you turn them over one by one with a click. Rare cards announce themselves face down: they glow in their rarity's color, and a Secret Rare or better stands in a beam of light. "Reveal all" turns the rest over, Space or a right click skips straight to all of them face up.
- **Structure Decks** put their cards straight into your binder.
- A **Collector's Tin** gives its promo card and three packs.

Carry a binder and every card you pull (from packs, a tin's promo, decks) goes straight into it, keeping its rarity; with several, the first one in your inventory. Without a binder the cards land in your inventory.
Packs and single cards turn up in dungeon, temple, mineshaft and treasure chests, mobs sometimes drop one, NPC duelists give one when you beat them, and the Card Trader sells them.
Hover over a card in your inventory, a chest, the binder or the deck box to see it big on the left, with its full text. A card you hold in your hand shows the same way in the top left corner.
# Foils
Rarer cards shine like the real ones: a Rare has a silver name, a Super Rare holofoil art, an Ultra Rare holofoil art and a gold name, a Secret Rare rainbow-lined art and a silver name.
# Alternate artworks

Some cards were printed with more than one artwork: Dark Magician, Blue-Eyes White Dragon, Red-Eyes Black Dragon and about a hundred more. A card from a pack or tin sometimes comes as one of its other artworks (chance {server:cards.altArtChance}, where 1 means always). An alt art shows its own picture everywhere, a gold ALT in the corner and "Alternate Art 2 of 8" in its tooltip.
It plays exactly like the original and counts as the same card: at most three of them together in a deck (fewer if the banlist says so), and one card in the Set Collection Book.
# Card Binder

Holds your collection. "Put all cards in" moves every loose card into it; clicking a card takes it out again (shift-click for every copy). It keeps each card's rarity, shown in the corner (R, SR, UR, ScR), and decks use commons first so your foils stay in the binder. Cards from sets that are still locked show a padlock.

**Searching:** just start typing when the binder opens. Every word has to turn up in the card's name, text, attribute or type, so dark dragon, tuner or quick-play all work (German type names like drache too); put words in quotes to find them as one phrase, like "destroy all". Right-click the box to clear it. The buttons below filter by card type, attribute, level and rarity (or only foils) and sort by name, ATK, DEF or level; shift-click steps back. The deck box's search works the same way.
[recipe {modid}:binder]
# Set Collection Book

Shows every set that is out (in a progression world, the sets unlocked so far) with how much of it you own: each card of the set counts once, whatever its rarity. It counts the cards in your binders, deck boxes and loose cards in your inventory and ender chest, also inside shulker boxes there. Open it with the book or `{cmd} sets`.
- The list shows each set's picture, your cards and a bar. Filter by started, complete, reward ready or not started, and sort by release, name or how complete; type a set's name or code to find it.
- Click a set to see its cards: the ones you're missing are greyed out, and a button shows only the missing ones.

- A complete set brings a reward once per player and set: {server:collection.pointsPerCard} DP per card of the set and {server:collection.packs} booster packs on this server. Click [Claim reward] (or "Claim all" for several). Everyone hears about it in chat.
[recipe {modid}:set_book]
# Collector displays

Show off your collection in your base. Right-click a display to open its slots: they take only cards (packs, decks and tins for the pack display), one per slot, and show them with their real pictures and foil. Shiny cards glow around their edge and sparkle, the rarer the more, and Secret Rares and up send a beam of light upward.
- **Card Frame**: one card behind glass, on a wall or lying on a table, with a name plate.
- **Card Showcase**: nine cards in three rows behind glass. Look at a card to see its name and rarity above it.
- **Toploader Stand**: one card standing in a toploader on your desk.
- **Pack Display**: an open display box with three sealed booster packs, structure decks or tins.

Whoever places a display owns it. New displays are **locked**: only the owner and operators can take things out or break it. The owner switches the lock and the light with the buttons in its window; with the light on it glows and its cards shine even in the dark. Name it in an anvil to put your own text on its name plate.
[recipe {modid}:card_frame]
[recipe {modid}:card_showcase]
[recipe {modid}:toploader_stand]
[recipe {modid}:pack_display]

chapters.title: Building decks
text: A **Deck Box** holds one deck. Right-click it: your cards are on the right, click one to add it; click a card in the deck on the left to put it back. Fusion, Synchro, Xyz and Link monsters go to the extra deck.
[recipe {modid}:deck_box]
# Deck rules
- 40 to 60 cards in the main deck, up to 15 in the extra deck.
- At most three copies of a card, fewer for cards on the banlist.

- In the Genesys format: no Link or Pendulum monsters, and the points of all cards (main, extra and side deck together) stay within the cap. The deck box shows the total next to the main deck, and each card with points shows its number in the top left corner.
- A deck box with a card that isn't allowed says which card is the problem.
# Finding cards
Search by name, filter by type (monsters, spells, traps, extra deck), attribute and level, and sort by name, ATK, DEF or level. Click a filter to step through it, shift-click to step back.
# Import and export
Export copies the deck as a YDK list, the format most deck builders read. Import replaces the deck with the YDK list in your clipboard, built from the cards you own, and says which ones were missing.

chapters.title: Shops and Duel Points
text: # Duel Points
Shops take **{server:shop.currency}** here ("points" means Duel Points, DP). DP are a balance, not an item: you see them above your inventory and in every shop, and `{cmd} dp` tells them.
- You start with {server:shop.points.startBalance} DP and get {server:shop.points.dailyBonus} DP once a day.

- Card Vending Machines buy loose cards ({server:shop.points.sellCommon} DP for a common up to {server:shop.points.sellSecret} for a Secret Rare) and emeralds ({server:shop.points.emeraldExchange} DP each).
- `{cmd} dp pay <player> <amount>` gives DP to someone else.

A DP shop shows its wares as tiles with the real product pictures; click one to see it large with its price, then Buy (or double-click it, or press Enter). Shift, or the second button, buys as many as you can afford. The Sell tab (Tab key) lists what the shop buys from you. Just start typing to search the shop, like the binder.
# Daily quests

**{key:quests}** or `{cmd} quests` opens your quests: {server:quests.daily} daily ones and {server:quests.weekly} weekly ones, such as "Win 2 duels with a Dragon deck" or "Fusion Summon 2 monsters". Each shows its progress and what it brings: Duel Points, booster packs and more.
- Duels count once they reach turn {server:quests.minTurns}. A pop-up in the corner shows when a quest moves on, and chat says when one is done.
- **Claim** each finished quest in the window, or **Claim all**. Rewards you forget are handed to you when new quests come.
- **Reroll** swaps an unfinished quest for another one, {server:quests.rerollsPerDay} times a day.
- New daily quests come every day at {server:quests.resetHour}:00 on the server's clock, new weekly ones on {server:quests.weeklyResetDay}.
- A "Deck: 6+ Dragon" quest counts duels with a deck holding at least that many such monsters.
# Trading

Swap cards and Duel Points with another player: `{cmd} trade <player>` asks them, or sneak and right-click them with a card, binder or deck box in your hand. They accept by clicking **[Accept]** in chat.

In the trade window you put your offer on the left and type your DP below it; on the right you see what the other player gives. The trade only happens once **both have confirmed**. Any change to either offer takes both confirmations back, and confirming then waits a moment, so nobody can swap something at the last second.
Cancelling, closing the window, logging out or a duel end the trade, and everyone gets their own offer back.
# Bounties

Put Duel Points on someone's head: `{cmd} bounty place <player> <amount>` (at least {server:bounty.minAmount} DP, plus a fee of {server:bounty.feePercent}%). The DP are taken right away and kept until someone collects them. Bounties from several players on the same player add up.

- Whoever **beats that player in a duel** collects the whole bounty; a winning tag team shares it. Only duels between people count, no bots or NPCs, and the duel has to reach turn {server:bounty.minTurns}.

- `{cmd} bounty` shows the biggest bounties, `{cmd} bounty <player>` who put what on someone. The player list (Tab) shows each bounty after the name, and a challenge tells you the bounty on your opponent.
- `{cmd} bounty withdraw <player>` takes your part back (not while they are dueling); the fee stays paid.
# Card Trader

A villager who sells binders, deck boxes, the starter decks and later a duel disk, plus packs, structure decks and tins: the newest {server:shop.newestAlways} products always and {server:shop.rotatingOlder} older ones that change every {server:shop.rotationDays} days. Any villager without a job takes it at a **Card Shop Counter**:
[recipe {modid}:card_shop]
# Card Vending Machine
The same shop without a villager: right-click it to buy. It also buys loose cards and emeralds for DP.
[recipe {modid}:card_machine]
# Shop Stand

A shop any player runs. As the owner, right-click it: put a ware in the top row and its price below it, then the wares themselves in the stock rows. Other players right-click it to buy, and what they pay goes to you, even while you're offline. Only you and operators can break it.
[recipe {modid}:shop_stand]

chapters.title: Progression and rules
text: This world plays with **{server:pool.mode}** cards.

- **progression**: a new world starts with {server:progression.startProduct}, and the next set unlocks by itself every {server:progression.daysPerSet} Minecraft days (0: only operators unlock them). Products come in release order. Locked cards show a padlock and can't go in a deck.
- **modeled**: the monsters with a 3D model, and the spells and traps of their era.
- **all**: every card, with packs from every booster.
# Rules over time

Duels follow the newest unlocked cards: Master Rule 1 until the first Xyz set, 2 until the first Pendulum set, 3 until the first Link set, 4 until April 2020, then 5, each with the banlist of its time. When two players at different steps duel, the one further along sets the rules.
# Banlists and Genesys

Instead of the list of its time the server can play with an official list: `tcg` (the newest TCG list), `ocg`, `traditional`, `worlds`, `master-duel`, or `genesys` and `genesys-ocg` for the **Genesys format**.

- **Genesys**: the banlist doesn't apply; instead some cards cost points. A deck may cost at most {server:genesysPointCap} points, and Link and Pendulum monsters are not allowed. Duels use today's rules on the original field, without Extra Monster Zones or Pendulum Zones.
- `{cmd} banlist` shows which list you play with and which lists there are.

- **Your own list:** an operator can give single players their own list, e.g. Genesys while the server plays TCG. A duel uses the list all duelists share; otherwise the challenger's, which the invitation names. Arena duels between players on different lists use the server's list, tournaments their own.

- Operators: `{cmd} banlist use <list>` picks the server's list (e.g. `genesys`), `{cmd} banlist use <list> <player>` gives players their own (`server` instead of a list takes it back), `{cmd} banlist update` downloads the newest official lists and uses them at once, without a restart, and `{cmd} banlist reset` goes back to the bundled ones. If a download fails, the list it had stays.
# For operators
- `{cmd} progression status`: the current set, rules, banlist and the next set, with the days until it unlocks.
- `{cmd} progression next [count]`: unlock the next set, or several.
- `{cmd} progression until <set or date>`: everything up to a set code such as MRL or a date such as 2005-03-01.
- `{cmd} progression set <set or date>`: like until, but can also go back.
- `{cmd} progression list [page]`: the sets in order, with what is unlocked (* marks a moved release date).

- `{cmd} progression date <set> <YYYY-MM-DD>`: gives a set another release date (`reset` brings back the real one); sets unlock in the order of their dates. `{cmd} progression date` lists the moved ones.

- With the Tycoon Calendar mod installed, sets come out when the world's calendar reaches their release date (`[progression] calendar` = {server:progression.calendar}). A calendar that starts later unlocks everything up to its start at once; setting it back takes nothing away.
With `[progression] scope` = {server:progression.scope}, "player" gives each player their own progress: add the player's name to the commands.

chapters.title: Arenas and tournaments
text: # Building your own arena

Build your arena from any blocks, as big or small as you like. The mod needs only two things: an **Arena Core** anywhere in the arena and a **Duelist Podium** where each duelist stands. One on each side, facing each other; two side by side for tag duels. Podiums may be up to 24 blocks from the core.

The field fits your build: it lies right between the podiums on your floor and turns with them. Its size follows the free floor: podiums far apart and plenty of room to the walls give a big field, a tight cellar a small one. Under a roof the monsters stay below it, and the duel mode camera stays in the room.
- **Right-click the core** to measure the arena and see the field's outline over the floor. Its window says whether the arena is ready and what is missing otherwise (a podium, or room for the field).
- **Field**: Fit room (as big as fits, at most {server:arena.maxFieldSize} times the usual size) or a fixed size from 50 to 200 %.
- **Podiums rise**: 0 to 5 blocks; the podiums carry the duelists up like pillars during a duel.
- **Look**: Holo mat (the glowing duel mat) or Outlines only (just the zone frames glow, so your floor shows).
Auto duels, tournaments, NPC opponents and spectators work in your own arenas just like in the Duel Arena. With two podiums a side, two pairs start a tag duel by themselves.
[recipe {modid}:duel_dome_core]
[recipe {modid}:duelist_platform]
# Duel Dome
A **Duel Dome Kit** builds a ready-made 13 by 21 arena on flat ground facing the way you look, with an Arena Core and four podiums. A good start to build on.
[recipe {modid}:duel_dome_kit]
# Duel Arena

A **Duel Arena Kit** builds the Duelist Kingdom arena out of ordinary blocks on flat ground: a platform with glass tiles, a red and a blue end with steps, posts and lamps, a Duelist Podium at each end and an Arena Core in the middle. When everyone stands on a podium, the field appears over the platform and the podiums lift the duelists 3 blocks up. An NPC opponent walks over to the free podium. Since it is all ordinary blocks, you can rebuild, decorate or enlarge it, and the core fits the field to it. It no longer packs back into its kit.

- **Auto duel**: step onto a podium and the arena shows **Waiting for Opponent...** until someone steps onto the other one. Then a {server:arena.countdownSeconds}-second countdown runs and the duel starts by itself, no invitation needed. Step off to call it off. You need a legal deck box (or the server lends a starter deck), and after a duel you step off and back on to go again. While a tournament is open, its arenas wait for its matches.
[recipe {modid}:duel_arena_kit]
# Tournaments

An operator opens a tournament with `{cmd} tournament create [format] [name]`, or the server opens them by itself on a schedule. Click **[Join]** in chat or use `{cmd} tournament join`. With `lockDeck` you play the whole tournament with the deck you joined with.
- **single**: single elimination; **double**: double elimination with a losers' bracket; **swiss**: Swiss rounds, with a top cut if set; **roundrobin**: everyone plays everyone.
- When registration closes, NPC duelists fill empty seats and the field is paired round by round.

- Matches are played only on Duel Arenas added with `{cmd} tournament arena add`. When your match is due you are brought onto a podium; click **[Ready]** to start sooner. Afterwards you go back to where you were.
- If you are offline or in another duel for {server:tournament.noShowMinutes} minutes when your match is due, you lose it.
`{cmd} tournament` opens the tournament window: bracket (drag to move it), table, matches, and rules and prizes. Entry fees are paid in the shop currency, and prizes replace the usual duel rewards.
# Draft & Sealed

In a Draft or Sealed tournament nobody brings a deck: everyone gets fresh packs at the start and builds a deck from them on the spot. The host opens one with `{cmd} tournament create sealed [name]` or `create draft [name]` (or sets `deckMode`). You join without a deck box.

- **Sealed**: everyone opens the same packs (`limitedPacks`, e.g. "pack 5" for five packs of a random set that is out, or "pack:lob 3; pack:mrd 2"). The packs are revealed one by one, then the deck building opens.

- **Draft**: everyone opens a pack, takes one card and passes the rest on, all at the same time: to the next duelist in the 1st, 3rd, ... pack, back the other way in the 2nd, 4th, ... Click a card to take it. After {server:tournament.pickSeconds} seconds a card is picked for you. NPCs draft too.

- **Deck building**: your deck on the left, the rest of your pool on the right. At least {server:tournament.deckMinimum} main deck cards, up to 15 in the extra deck, as many copies as you pulled, no banlist. **Auto** builds a deck from your best cards, **Done** locks it in. After {server:tournament.buildMinutes} minutes whoever isn't done plays an automatically built deck.
- Once all decks are done, the bracket is drawn and the matches run as in any tournament. With `keepCards` on, you keep your pool afterwards; otherwise the cards are only lent for the tournament.
`{cmd} tournament deck` opens the draft or deck building window again if you closed it.
# Star Chips

A **Star Chip event** is Duelist Kingdom on your server. An operator starts one with `{cmd} starchips start [name]`; click **[Join]** in chat or use `{cmd} starchips join` and you get {server:starchips.startChips} Star Chips.

- Every 1v1 duel with another duelist of the event is for Star Chips: each side puts up {server:starchips.defaultWager}, or more with `{cmd} starchips duel <player> <chips>`. The winner takes them all. Duels on Duel Arena podiums count too. Duels against NPC duelists only count if the server turns on `npcDuels` ({server:starchips.npcDuels}).
- Collect **{server:starchips.goal}** to qualify for the finals. Lose your last chip and you are out.
- The **Duelist Glove** in the top left corner shows your chips. `{cmd} starchips` shows everyone's.

- Once {server:starchips.finalists} have qualified (or time runs out, or an operator runs `{cmd} starchips finals`), the finals are held as a tournament on the tournament arenas, with the prizes from `finalsSettings`. Empty seats go to the duelists with the most chips.

chapters.title: Clans
text: Duelists band together in **clans**: a tag in your clan's color in front of your name, a crest, a clan treasury and a clan ranking, and clan wars against other clans.
**{key:clan}** or `{cmd} clan` opens the clan window: your clan, its wars and the clan ranking. Its buttons run the same commands as below.
# Founding and joining
- `{cmd} clan create <tag> <name>` founds a clan (costs {server:clans.createPrice} DP). The tag is 2 to 5 letters or digits, like KC.
- The leader and officers invite with `{cmd} clan invite <player>`; the invited player clicks **[Join]** or uses `{cmd} clan join <tag>`. An open clan (`{cmd} clan open true`) takes anyone.
- A clan holds up to {server:clans.maxMembers} members (0 means no limit). `{cmd} clan leave` leaves it.

- **Roles:** the **leader** runs everything; **officers** invite, remove members, set the crest and motto and answer war declarations; **members** duel and pay in. The leader promotes with `{cmd} clan promote <member>`, demotes with `demote` and hands over the lead with `{cmd} clan leader <member>`.
# Tag, crest and treasury

- Every member's tag stands in front of their name in chat, in the player list and above their head (`showTag`: {server:clans.showTag}). The leader picks the color with the **Color** button in the clan window or `{cmd} clan color <color>`.

- **Crest:** make a banner on a loom, hold it and run `{cmd} clan crest`. Its colors and patterns become the crest in the clan window and the ranking. `{cmd} clan banner` gives you a copy ({server:clans.bannerPrice} DP).

- **FTB Teams:** when the server has FTB Teams, every clan is also an FTB Teams party with the same members, leader, officers, name, color and motto, so chunk claims, quests and team chat of FTB mods count for the whole clan (`ftbTeams`: {server:clans.ftbTeams}). Joining or leaving the party joins or leaves the clan and the other way round. If you own a party, founding a clan turns it into the clan; disbanding a clan keeps its party.
- **Treasury:** members pay Duel Points in with `{cmd} clan deposit <amount>`. It pays for war stakes; the leader pays out with `{cmd} clan withdraw <amount>` or `{cmd} clan pay <member> <amount>`.
- `{cmd} clan chat <message>` talks to your clan only.
# Clan wars

The leader or an officer declares war from the clan ranking (pick a clan) or with `{cmd} clan war declare <tag> race|battle [stake]`. The other clan has {server:clans.warAcceptHours} hours to accept (**[Accept]** in chat or `{cmd} clan war accept`). Each side puts up the same stake from its treasury (at most {server:clans.maxStake} DP); the winner takes both and {server:clans.warWinPoints} DP more.

- **Race for points:** for {server:clans.warHours} hours, every duel a member wins against a member of the other clan is a point. First to {server:clans.warTarget} points wins early; otherwise whoever is ahead when the time is up. The same two duelists count {server:clans.warMaxPerPair} times at most, so beat many of them. Tag duels count when each side is from one clan. Only ranked duels count: {server:clans.warOnlyRanked}.

- **Arena battle:** each clan names {server:clans.battleDuelists} duelists (`{cmd} clan war join`, or the leader with `{cmd} clan war lineup <names>`). Once both say `{cmd} clan war ready`, they fight one bout after another on a tournament arena, first against first: each duelist is brought onto a podium, the bout starts after {server:clans.battleCallSeconds} seconds, and afterwards everyone goes back. Every bout won is a point. A duelist who doesn't show up within {server:clans.battleNoShowMinutes} minutes loses the bout.
- `{cmd} clan war` shows how your wars stand; the leader can give up with `{cmd} clan war surrender`. After a war the same two clans rest {server:clans.warCooldownHours} hours.
# Clan ranking

Every clan starts at a rating of {server:clans.startRating}. Winning a war takes rating from the loser, more for beating a stronger clan (up to {server:clans.kFactor} a war). The clan window lists the clans by rating with their crest and war record; `{cmd} clan top` shows the ten best in chat, `{cmd} clan info <tag>` one clan.

chapters.title: NPC duelists
text: Duelists wander the overworld now and then, each with a title, a duel disk and their own deck: a famous tournament deck whose era has come, a starter or structure deck that is out, or a random deck from the card pool. They say which deck they play.
Right-click one to duel it. Beat it and it won't duel you again for {server:results.npcs.rematchMinutes} minutes. NPCs can't be hurt while dueling.

They play with WindBot, the well-known AI from YGOPro, in one of four styles: balanced, aggressive (summons and attacks a lot), defensive (sets monsters, shows only strong ones) or control (spends removal freely). Each NPC keeps its style, and like beginners they now and then let a response or an attack go by. A **Duelist Spawn Egg** is in the creative tab.

chapters.title: Cosmetics and Figura
text: **{key:cosmetics}** or `{cmd} cosmetics` opens the cosmetics menu:
- **Disk skins**: Battle City, Slifer Red, Ra Yellow, Obelisk Blue, Shadow, Crimson and Gold. The skin is stored on the disk, so it goes wherever the disk goes.
- **Card sleeves**: Classic, Crimson, Emerald, Amethyst, Onyx and Gold. Your opponent sees them on your face-down cards and piles.
Locked ones say how to unlock them: winning duels, beating NPC duelists or opening booster packs.
# Figura
With the Figura mod installed, avatar scripts can react to duels and draw their own duel disk. A ready-made starter avatar is a separate download next to the mod.

chapters.title: Commands
text: # For everyone
- `{cmd} guide`: this book.
- `{cmd} duel bot`: duel the computer.
- `{cmd} duel <player>`: challenge someone, add `ante` for an ante duel.
- `{cmd} accept`: accept a challenge.
- `{cmd} forfeit`: surrender the duel.
- `{cmd} tag <partner> <opponent1> <opponent2>`: tag duel, any seat can be `bot`.
- `{cmd} battlecity <partner> <opponent1> <opponent2>`: tag duel on split halves.
- `{cmd} watch [player]` and `{cmd} unwatch`: watch a duel (without a name, the one you stand near) and stop.
- `{cmd} stats [player]` and `{cmd} stats top`: duel records.
- `{cmd} duel <player> ranked`: a ranked duel; `{cmd} rank`, `{cmd} rank <player>` and `{cmd} rank top`: the ranking.
- `{cmd} clan`: the clan window; `{cmd} clan create|invite|join|leave|chat|deposit|banner|info|top` and `{cmd} clan war declare|accept|deny|join|ready|surrender`: clans and clan wars (see Clans).
- `{cmd} dp` and `{cmd} dp pay <player> <amount>`: your Duel Points, and giving some away.
- `{cmd} trade <player>`: ask someone to trade; `{cmd} trade accept [player]` and `deny [player]`: accept or decline a request.
- `{cmd} bounty`, `{cmd} bounty <player>`, `{cmd} bounty place <player> <amount>` and `withdraw <player>`: bounties.
- `{cmd} shop`: the vending machine's shop from anywhere, if the server allows it.
- `{cmd} starter`: pick your first deck if you haven't yet.
- `{cmd} sets`: the Set Collection Book.
- `{cmd} quests`: your daily and weekly quests.
- `{cmd} cosmetics`: disk skins and card sleeves.
- `{cmd} version`: the version of the rules engine.
- `{cmd} banlist`: which banlist you play with.
# Tournaments
- `{cmd} tournament`: the tournament window; `bracket`, `table`, `matches` and `rules` open it at that tab.
- `{cmd} tournament join`, `leave` and `ready`: take part, drop out, start your match.
- `{cmd} tournament deck`: the draft or deck building window of a Draft or Sealed tournament.
- `{cmd} tournament status` and `settings`: where it stands and what it plays with.
- Hosts: `{cmd} tournament create [format] [name]`, `set <setting> <value>`, `start`, `cancel`, `addnpc [count]`, `kick <name>`.
# Star Chips
- `{cmd} starchips`: the standings of the Star Chip event.
- `{cmd} starchips join` and `leave`: take part (with fresh chips) and drop out (your chips are gone).
- `{cmd} starchips duel <player> [chips]`: challenge another duelist of the event for more chips each.
- Hosts: `{cmd} starchips start [name]`, `finals` (begin the finals now), `cancel`, `kick <name>`.
# For operators
- `{cmd} progression status`, `next [count]`, `until <set>`, `set <set>` and `list [page]`: see Progression and rules.
- `{cmd} dp <player>` and `{cmd} dp give|take|set <players> <amount>`: look at and change Duel Points.
- `{cmd} stats reset <player>`: clear a duel record.
- `{cmd} rank set <player> <rating>`, `{cmd} rank reset <player>` and `{cmd} rank season confirm` (a new season: everyone back to the start rating).
- `{cmd} clan admin disband <tag>`, `rating <tag> <rating>`, `treasury <tag> <amount>`, `endwar <tag>` (ends a war on the current score) and `season confirm` (every clan back to the start rating).
- `{cmd} bounty clear <player>`: call off a bounty; everyone gets back what they put up.

- `{cmd} quests reload`: read `config/{modid}/quests.json` again; `{cmd} quests list`: every quest of the pool; `{cmd} quests reset <player>`: new quests for someone; `{cmd} quests complete <player> <quest>`: finish one of theirs.
- `{cmd} tournament arena add`, `arena remove [number]` and `arena list`: the Duel Arenas tournaments play on (stand on one to add it); `{cmd} tournament award <name>`: decide a match.
- `{cmd} starchips give|take|set <name> <amount>`: change someone's Star Chips.
- `{cmd} gallery [page]`: lays out a page of monster models to look at; `{cmd} gallery clear` removes them.
- `{cmd} joindecks give <player>`: gives someone all their decks from `config/{modid}/join_decks/` again (see Settings).

- `{cmd} banlist update`: download the newest official banlists and Genesys points; `{cmd} banlist use <list> [player]`: pick one for the server or for players (`server` gives them the server's again); `{cmd} banlist reset`: back to the bundled ones (see Progression and rules).
# Admin menu
**{key:admin}** or `{cmd} admin` opens the admin menu for operators (level 2, like `/give`). Top right picks who for: you, another player or everyone online.
- **Products**: every booster pack, structure deck and tin, searched by name or set code, or a random pack. Click gives the count you set.
- **Cards**: any card by name or passcode, in any rarity, locked ones too. Alternate artworks come right after their card.
- **Duel Points**: type an amount, then give, take or set; below are the balances of everyone online.
Everything runs on the server and shows up like a command in the operators' chat and the server log.

chapters.title: Settings
text: # Server settings
In the world folder: `serverconfig/{modid}-server.toml`. Edit it with the world closed or the server stopped. Green values are the current ones.
- `ruleset` = {server:ruleset}: auto (follows the cards, see Progression; Genesys with a Genesys list), mr1, goat, mr2, mr3, mr4, modern or genesys.
- `banlist` = {server:banlist}: auto, none, an official list (tcg, ocg, traditional, worlds, master-duel, genesys, genesys-ocg), or a file in `config/{modid}/banlists/`.
- `genesysPointCap` = {server:genesysPointCap}: how many Genesys points a deck may cost. Tournaments can have their own cap (`genesysPointCap`).
- `startingLifePoints` = {server:startingLifePoints}: life points at the start of a 1v1 duel.
- `tagStartingLifePoints` = {server:tagStartingLifePoints}: each team's life points at the start of a tag or Battle City duel (2v2).
- `allowAnte` = {server:allowAnte}: ante duels allowed.
- `turnTimeLimit` = {server:turnTimeLimit}: seconds per person and turn, 0 for none. Afterwards the computer plays the rest of the turn.
- `starterDecksWithoutDeckBox` = {server:starterDecksWithoutDeckBox}: players without a legal deck box duel with a starter deck.
- `packsIntoBinder` = {server:packsIntoBinder}: cards from opened packs, tins and decks go straight into the binder you carry.

- `[ai] engine` = {server:ai.engine}: windbot or classic (the older AI). `npcStyle` = {server:ai.npcStyle} and `npcMistakes` = {server:ai.npcMistakes} for NPC duelists, `botStyle` = {server:ai.botStyle} and `botMistakes` = {server:ai.botMistakes} for tournament bots, bot seats and the stand-in for players out of time. Styles: balanced, aggressive, defensive, control or random; mistakes: 0 to 1.
- `[pool] mode` = {server:pool.mode}: progression, modeled or all.
- `[progression] scope` = {server:progression.scope}: one progress for the server, or one per player.
- `[progression] startProduct` = {server:progression.startProduct}: where new worlds or players start.
- `[progression] announce` = {server:progression.announce}: say unlocks in chat.
- `[progression] daysPerSet` = {server:progression.daysPerSet}: Minecraft days until the next set unlocks by itself; 0 leaves it to operators.
- `[progression] calendar` = {server:progression.calendar}: with the Tycoon Calendar mod, sets come out on their release date by the world's calendar instead.
- `[progression] releaseDates`: sets released on other days, e.g. `["MRD=2002-04-01"]`; `{cmd} progression date` changes them in game.
- `[cards] lockedInDeck` = {server:cards.lockedInDeck}: locked cards stay out of decks.
- `[cards] altArtChance` = {server:cards.altArtChance}: how often a card from a pack or tin comes as one of its alternate artworks (0 never, 1 always).

- `[results] trackRecord` = {server:results.trackRecord}, `announce` = {server:results.announce}, `rewardBotDuels` = {server:results.rewardBotDuels}: duel records, results in chat, rewards for bot duels.

- `[results.players]` and `[results.npcs]`: `winPacks`, `winPoints`, `winEmeralds`, `winXp`, `lossPacks`, `lossPoints`, `lossEmeralds`, `lossXp` (see Dueling; DP only with points as the currency); `[results.npcs] rematchMinutes` = {server:results.npcs.rematchMinutes}.

- `[shop] currency` = {server:shop.currency}: "points" or an item such as minecraft:emerald. `priceMultiplier` = {server:shop.priceMultiplier}, `dynamicPrices` = {server:shop.dynamicPrices}, `wanderingTrader` = {server:shop.wanderingTrader}.
- `[shop] newestAlways` = {server:shop.newestAlways}, `rotatingOlder` = {server:shop.rotatingOlder}, `rotationDays` = {server:shop.rotationDays}: the Card Trader's stock.
- `[shop.prices]` and `[shop.stock]`: what everything costs (0 stops a trade) and how many a trader has.

- `[shop.machine]`: `enabled` = {server:shop.machine.enabled}, `products` = {server:shop.machine.products}, `limitPerPlayer` = {server:shop.machine.limitPerPlayer}, `command` = {server:shop.machine.command}, `operatorsOnly` = {server:shop.machine.operatorsOnly}.

- `[shop.players]`: `enabled` = {server:shop.players.enabled}, `maxPerPlayer` = {server:shop.players.maxPerPlayer}, `taxPercent` = {server:shop.players.taxPercent}, `currencyOnly` = {server:shop.players.currencyOnly}.

- `[shop.points]`: `startBalance` = {server:shop.points.startBalance}, `dailyBonus` = {server:shop.points.dailyBonus}, `pricePoints` = {server:shop.points.pricePoints} (DP per 1 of a price), `transfers` = {server:shop.points.transfers}, `emeraldExchange` = {server:shop.points.emeraldExchange}, `sellCommon` to `sellSecret`.

- `[tournament]`: the defaults of every new tournament; its host can change them with `{cmd} tournament set`. `format` = {server:tournament.format}, `bestOf` = {server:tournament.bestOf}, `minPlayers` = {server:tournament.minPlayers}, `maxPlayers` = {server:tournament.maxPlayers}, `registrationMinutes` = {server:tournament.registrationMinutes}, `npcFill` = {server:tournament.npcFill}, `lockDeck` = {server:tournament.lockDeck}, `entryFee` = {server:tournament.entryFee}, `potShare` = {server:tournament.potShare}, `prizesFirst` to `prizesEveryone`, and more (`{cmd} tournament settings` lists them).
- `[tournament] playersCanHost` = {server:tournament.playersCanHost}: players may host. `schedule`: times such as "20:00" or "SAT 18:30" when tournaments open by themselves.
- `[guide] giveOnFirstJoin` = {server:guide.giveOnFirstJoin} and `craftable` = {server:guide.craftable}: this book.
- `[arena] autoStart` = {server:arena.autoStart}: a duel starts by itself when one player stands on each podium of a Duel Arena, after `countdownSeconds` = {server:arena.countdownSeconds}.

- `[arena] maxFieldSize` = {server:arena.maxFieldSize} and `minFieldSize` = {server:arena.minFieldSize}: how big the field in a player-built arena may get at most, and how little room still works (1 is the usual size).

- `[ranking] enabled` = {server:ranking.enabled}, `startRating` = {server:ranking.startRating}, `kFactor` = {server:ranking.kFactor} (the most points one duel moves), `placementGames` = {server:ranking.placementGames}, `tiers` = {server:ranking.tiers} (where Silver to Duel King start), `promotionPoints` = {server:ranking.promotionPoints}, `maxPerPairPerDay` = {server:ranking.maxPerPairPerDay}, `arenaDuels` = {server:ranking.arenaDuels} (Duel Arena auto duels are ranked), `showInTabList` = {server:ranking.showInTabList}, `announcePromotions` = {server:ranking.announcePromotions}. Tournaments are ranked with their own setting `ranked`.

- `[clans]`: `enabled` = {server:clans.enabled}, `createPrice` = {server:clans.createPrice}, `maxMembers` = {server:clans.maxMembers}, `bannerPrice` = {server:clans.bannerPrice}, `showTag` = {server:clans.showTag}, `ftbTeams` = {server:clans.ftbTeams}, `startRating` = {server:clans.startRating}, `kFactor` = {server:clans.kFactor}, `warHours` = {server:clans.warHours}, `warTarget` = {server:clans.warTarget}, `warMaxPerPair` = {server:clans.warMaxPerPair}, `warOnlyRanked` = {server:clans.warOnlyRanked}, `warAcceptHours` = {server:clans.warAcceptHours}, `warCooldownHours` = {server:clans.warCooldownHours}, `warMinMembers` = {server:clans.warMinMembers}, `maxStake` = {server:clans.maxStake}, `warWinPoints` = {server:clans.warWinPoints}, `announceWars` = {server:clans.announceWars}, `battleDuelists` = {server:clans.battleDuelists}, `battleCallSeconds` = {server:clans.battleCallSeconds}, `battleNoShowMinutes` = {server:clans.battleNoShowMinutes}. See the Clans chapter.

- `[trade]`: `enabled` = {server:trade.enabled}, `onlyModItems` = {server:trade.onlyModItems} (only this mod's items), `points` = {server:trade.points} (DP in trades, needs `transfers`), `maxDistance` = {server:trade.maxDistance} (blocks, 0 for anywhere), `requestSeconds` = {server:trade.requestSeconds}, `rightClick` = {server:trade.rightClick} (sneak-right-click asks).

- `[bounty]`: `enabled` = {server:bounty.enabled}, `minAmount` = {server:bounty.minAmount}, `feePercent` = {server:bounty.feePercent}, `minTurns` = {server:bounty.minTurns} (the turn a duel has to reach), `withdraw` = {server:bounty.withdraw}, `announce` = {server:bounty.announce}, `showInTabList` = {server:bounty.showInTabList}.

- `[collection]`: what a complete set in the Set Collection Book brings, once per player: `pointsPerCard` = {server:collection.pointsPerCard} (DP per card of the set, with points as the currency), `packs` = {server:collection.packs}, `emeralds` = {server:collection.emeralds}, `xp` = {server:collection.xp}; `announce` = {server:collection.announce}: tell everyone in chat.

- `[starchips]`: `startChips` = {server:starchips.startChips}, `goal` = {server:starchips.goal}, `finalists` = {server:starchips.finalists}, `defaultWager` = {server:starchips.defaultWager}, `maxWager` = {server:starchips.maxWager} (0: no limit), `npcDuels` = {server:starchips.npcDuels}, `npcWager` = {server:starchips.npcWager}, `durationMinutes` = {server:starchips.durationMinutes} (0: until enough qualify), `fillFinals` = {server:starchips.fillFinals}, `lateJoin` = {server:starchips.lateJoin}, `entryFee` = {server:starchips.entryFee} Duel Points, `playersCanHost` = {server:starchips.playersCanHost}, `announce` = {server:starchips.announce}. `finalsSettings`: tournament settings for the finals such as "bestOf=3" or "prizesFirst=pack 10; points 1000".
# Decks for particular players

A YDK deck list in `config/{modid}/join_decks/<UUID>/` (or as `config/{modid}/join_decks/<UUID>.ydk`) becomes a deck box with those cards for the player with that UUID on their next join, once per world. The deck box is named after the file; a file added later is given on the next join. Unknown passcodes are left out and named in chat. The mod's author gets his own deck, which comes with the mod, on every server; `bundledJoinDecks` = {server:bundledJoinDecks} turns that off.

- `[quests]`: `enabled` = {server:quests.enabled}, `daily` = {server:quests.daily}, `weekly` = {server:quests.weekly}, `sameForEveryone` = {server:quests.sameForEveryone} (everyone gets the same quests, no rerolls), `rerollsPerDay` = {server:quests.rerollsPerDay}, `resetHour` = {server:quests.resetHour}, `weeklyResetDay` = {server:quests.weeklyResetDay}, `minTurns` = {server:quests.minTurns}, `botDuels` = {server:quests.botDuels}, `announceWeekly` = {server:quests.announceWeekly}. The quests themselves, their goals and rewards are in `config/{modid}/quests.json`: add, change or remove any, then `{cmd} quests reload`.
# Your own settings
In `config/{modid}-client.toml`:
- `downloadCardArt` = {client:downloadCardArt}: card art is downloaded on first view and kept on your computer. `cardArtUrl` and `cardArtCroppedUrl` say where from.
- `realProductImages` = {client:realProductImages}: booster packs, decks and tins show the real product, its picture downloaded the same way. `productImageUrl` says where from.
- `chooseZone` = {client:chooseZone}: pick the zone yourself when playing a card from its menu.
- `skipResponses` = {client:skipResponses}: pass every response you don't have to take (switch it in a duel with {key:duel_responses}).
- `cardPreview` = {client:cardPreview}: a big picture of the card under the mouse, with its text, left of the inventory, chests, the binder and the deck box, and of a card in your hand.
- `packOpeningShow` = {client:packOpeningShow}: open booster packs as a show (tear open, fan, turn each card over). Off, the cards just turn over in rows.
- `fieldSpellArena` = {client:fieldSpellArena}: face-up Field Spells transform the duel field.
- `displayEffects` = {client:displayEffects}: shiny cards in collector displays glow and sparkle, with a beam for Secret Rares and up.

- `aceCamera` = {client:aceCamera}: when a big monster is summoned, the camera circles it for two seconds and its name shows big. Every monster of Level `aceMinLevel` = {client:aceMinLevel} or higher counts, with at least `aceMinAttack` = {client:aceMinAttack} ATK (0: off), or from the Extra Deck (`aceExtraDeck` = {client:aceExtraDeck}).
- `longSummonShows` = {client:longSummonShows}: the full show (about 2.5 seconds) for a Fusion, Synchro, Xyz, Ritual, Link or Pendulum Summon; off, 1.5 seconds.
- `finisherCamera` = {client:finisherCamera}: swing the camera round to whoever takes the final blow of a duel while it plays in slow motion.

chapters.title: Tips
text: - Monsters without a 3D model stand on the field as a hologram of their artwork. A resource pack can give any monster a model.

- Destroyed cards shatter into shards of their picture, and every card that leaves the field flies to where it goes. The blow that ends a duel plays in slow motion, and the winner gets fireworks over their half (in their clan's color).
- Card art needs an internet connection the first time a card is shown; after that it comes from your computer.
- Can't put a card in your deck? It is from a set that is still locked, or the banlist limits it. The deck box tells you which.
- An ante duel's cards are safe: a crash or restart gives them back, and a winner who logged off gets them on the next login.
- In a 2v2 duel only the partner whose turn it is answers prompts; both see the team's hand.
- Lost this book? `{cmd} guide` opens it, or craft a new one from a book and paper.

- For servers with KubeJS: scripts can react to duels, packs, tournaments and ranks (`JadmEvents`) and give cards, packs and Duel Points (`Jadm`). The guide is `docs/kubejs.md` in the mod's GitHub repository.
